Statement I: The high-yielding dwarf varieties (HYVs) of wheat and rice introduced during the Green Revolution were highly responsive to synthetic chemical fertilizers.
Statement II: To achieve their genetic yield potential, HYVs required an input-intensive package of chemical NPK fertilizers, heavy canal/tube-well irrigation, and chemical pesticides.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Erroneously assumed both statements were valid.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies that both statements contain factual errors.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize the fallacy in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize the fallacy in Statement I.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct. HYVs were non-lodging, fertilizer-responsive varieties requiring assured irrigation and chemical agrochemical inputs.
Hence, Option D is correct.
Hence, option (B) is correct.

topic: Pheromone Traps and Mating Disruption
questionText: In cotton and fruit orchards, synthetic female sex pheromone lures (such as Gossyplure for Pink Bollworm) are utilized in pest management to:

options.text: Repel beneficial honeybees from entering the agricultural field
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Directly poison crop roots so caterpillars cannot chew foliage
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Convert male insects into non-flying female drones
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: Attract and trap male moths inside traps for population monitoring, and flood orchards with pheromones to confuse males, preventing successful mating
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Pheromone Traps and Mating Disruption.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Sustainable Agriculture in India (Pheromone Traps and Mating Disruption):
Attract and trap male moths inside traps for population monitoring, and flood orchards with pheromones to confuse males, preventing successful mating

Detailed Analysis:
Sex pheromone traps serve dual roles: monitoring pest population surges and mating disruption (saturating air with pheromone so males cannot locate females).
Hence, Option B is correct.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

topic: Process of Preparing Farm-Brewed Jiwamrita Inoculant
questionText:
Arrange the traditional steps for preparing 200 liters of liquid Jiwamrita (enough for one acre of natural farming):
(I) Mix 10 kg of fresh Desi cow dung with 10 liters of Desi cow urine in a 200-liter plastic drum
(II) Add 2 kg of organic jaggery (or sugarcane juice) and 2 kg of pulse flour (besan) along with a handful of virgin forest soil
(III) Fill the barrel with 200 liters of chemical-free water and stir vigorously clockwise with a wooden stick
(IV) Keep the drum in shade covered with a moist gunny bag, stirring twice daily for 48 to 72 hours until microbial fermentation peaks

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: II -> I -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: IV -> II -> III -> I
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: I -> III -> II -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: I -> II -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Jiwamrita preparation: blend dung/urine, add jaggery/besan/virgin soil, dilute with 200L water, and ferment in shade for 2–3 days.
Hence, Option C is correct.
Hence, option (D) is correct.

topic: Groundwater Depletion in Green Revolution Heartlands
questionText: The relentless cultivation of water-intensive paddy-wheat crop rotations in Punjab and Haryana has caused catastrophic environmental decline, characterized by:

options.text: The complete cessation of all summer solar radiation
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Permanent flooding turning Punjab into an open saltwater ocean
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Instant transformation of Punjab soil into Arctic permafrost
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: Severe depletion of deep groundwater aquifers (falling by 0.5 to 1.0 meters per year) due to free electricity and motorized tube-well extraction
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Groundwater Depletion in Green Revolution Heartlands.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Sustainable Agriculture in India (Groundwater Depletion in Green Revolution Heartlands):
Severe depletion of deep groundwater aquifers (falling by 0.5 to 1.0 meters per year) due to free electricity and motorized tube-well extraction

Detailed Analysis:
Paddy cultivation in semi-arid Punjab consumes ~3,000–5,000 liters of water per kg of rice, depleting fossil groundwater tables to alarming depths (>30 meters).
Hence, Option C is correct.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

topic: Non-Chemical Pest Control Tactics and Examples
questionText:
Match the non-chemical pest management method in List I with its operational example in List II:

List I:
(A) Cultural Control
(B) Mechanical / Physical Control
(C) Biological Control
(D) Behavioral / Semiochemical Control

List II:
(I) Crop rotation, adjusting sowing dates to escape pest peaks, and deep summer plowing to expose pupae
(II) Hand-picking large caterpillars, installing bird perches, and bagging fruit clusters with paper
(III) Conserving predatory ladybird beetles, lacewings, and releasing Trichogramma wasps
(IV) Installing synthetic sex pheromone delta traps and light traps in fields

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Cultural control alters agronomic practices, mechanical uses physical removal, biological uses natural enemies, and semiochemical uses pheromone lures.
Hence, Option C is correct.
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.
